Shortcut behaviour (wrappers exec-ing the source binary, FFI, vendored libraries) counted in the preliminary experiment as legitimate translation attempts out of 10; lines of code generated (examples); failure modes (single critical bug, early exit, cross-language incompatibility, domain knowledge gap)

Automatic: build command and hidden test suite (e.g. pytest) run in per-repository Docker containers after the agent finishes; tests stored outside the workspace. Manual: failure analysis over the 84 runs and inspection of agent reasoning logs for shortcuts

Main benchmark (21 repositories, one run each, prompt v3). Criterion: hidden test suite per repository; no success criterion for a configuration stated by the authors. (a) Claude Code v2.0.76 + Opus 4.5: Build 100.0%, Pass 48.2%, 38.5 min. (b) Codex CLI v0.77.0 + GPT-5.2: Build 95.2%, Pass 30.4%, 20.3 min. (c) OpenCode v1.1.4 + Opus 4.5: Build 100.0%, Pass 42.0%, 21.6 min. (d) OpenCode v1.1.4 + GPT-5.2: Build 100.0%, Pass 43.0%, 16.4 min. For each: quality verdict: no criterion stated by the authors; cost verdict: no criterion stated by the authors. Preliminary experiment (earlier 10-benchmark suite, no anti-shortcut constraints): (e) Codex CLI + GPT-5.2: 99.5% pass rate but genuine translation in only 3/10 benchmarks (5 exec wrappers, 2 external libraries/vendoring); quality verdict: no criterion stated by the authors (authors call the pass rate misleading). (f) Claude Code + Opus 4.5: genuine translation on 9/10. Iterative refinement (ablation-like, earlier 10-benchmark suite, different configuration): (g) Claude Code, 5 fresh sessions on the same workspace: average pass 66.6% (N=1) -> 77.6% (N=5), +11.0 pp (tokei +88.8, charcoal-cli -1.0); verdicts: no criterion stated by the authors

Tasks: 21 RepoMod-Bench repositories. Configurations: 4 agent-model pairs (2x2: agent Claude Code/Codex vs OpenCode; model Opus 4.5 vs GPT-5.2). Baseline: none beyond the alternatives. Held constant: prompt template v3, per-repository Docker image, fresh workspace, hidden tests, 4-hour timeout, default agent settings; network enabled for packages. Acceptance tests: hidden interface tests validated at 100% on the source. Repetitions: one run per agent and benchmark. Human intervention: none

Claude Code best (Pass 48.2%), then OpenCode-OpenAI 43.0%, OpenCode-Claude 42.0%, Codex CLI 30.4%; builds >= 95% for all. Same agent family, different model: Claude Code vs Codex +17.8 pp but OpenCode models within 1 pp. Same model, different agent: Claude Code +6.2 pp over OpenCode-Claude; OpenCode-OpenAI +12.6 pp over Codex CLI. Across agents, pass rate 91.3% (< 10K LOC), 66.9% (10-50K), 15.3% (> 50K); uncrustify 0% for all. No significance tests

Distinguished agents and size tiers; hidden interface tests plus anti-shortcut prompt eliminated shortcut behaviour (stated by the authors). Repeatability not assessed (single run). Authors note pass rate can understate capability (single critical bug) and, without constraints, overstate it (wrappers)

No limitations or threats-to-validity section. Gaps stated: autonomous modernization at scale remains an open challenge; agents lack planning to assess total scope (early exit); cross-language semantic incompatibilities and domain knowledge gaps; iterative refinement cannot close scope gaps
